I ported the server to plain Kotlin with no third-party dependencies. `node check.mjs` builds it and passes all 4 example cases.

I also tested a few things by hand on a random port:
- A 1 MiB value stores and comes back byte-for-byte; one byte over that gets `413`.
- Bad keys get `400`: empty, 65 characters long, containing a `/`, or with any other character. Unknown paths get `404`.
- An empty value works.
- 300 PUTs sent 64 at a time all returned `201`, and `GET /kv` listed every key.

How it
